# PaycheckEstimates.com

> Free US Paycheck Calculator — Calculate your exact take-home pay after federal tax, state tax, Social Security, and Medicare deductions for all 50 US states. Updated for 2026 tax rates.

## About
PaycheckEstimates.com is a free online paycheck calculator for US employees and workers. It provides instant, accurate take-home pay calculations after all federal and state tax deductions using the latest 2026 tax brackets and rates. No signup required. Works for all 50 US states plus Washington D.C.

## Primary Tool
- Paycheck Calculator: https://paycheckestimates.com/

## Supporting Pages

- Contact: https://paycheckestimates.com/contact.html

## What This Tool Does
PaycheckEstimates.com calculates US take-home pay by applying:
- 2026 Federal income tax brackets (10%, 12%, 22%, 24%, 32%, 35%, 37%)
- State income tax rates for all 50 states and Washington D.C.
- Social Security tax (6.2% up to $176,100 wage base)
- Medicare tax (1.45% on all wages, 0.9% additional on wages over $200,000)
- Pre-tax deductions including 401(k) contributions and health insurance premiums

## Supported Inputs
- Annual salary or hourly wage
- Pay frequency: weekly, bi-weekly, semi-monthly, monthly, annually
- Filing status: Single, Married Filing Jointly, Head of Household
- All 50 US states and Washington D.C.
- Pre-tax deductions: 401(k) percentage, health insurance per paycheck

## Output
- Net take-home pay per paycheck, monthly, and annually
- Breakdown of all deductions: federal tax, state tax, Social Security, Medicare
- Effective tax rate
- Visual bar breakdown of each deduction

## Key Questions This Tool Answers
- How much of my paycheck goes to taxes?
- What is my take-home pay after federal and state taxes?
- How do I calculate my net pay from gross salary?
- How much Social Security and Medicare tax is taken from my paycheck?
- What is the difference between gross pay and net pay?
- Which US states have no income tax?
- How does filing status affect my paycheck?
- How much does a 401k contribution reduce my taxes?
- What are the federal tax brackets for 2026?
- How do I calculate my effective tax rate?

## Tax Data Used (2026)
Federal standard deductions: Single $15,000 / Married $30,000 / Head of Household $22,500

Federal tax brackets (Single filer):
- 10%: $0 to $11,925
- 12%: $11,926 to $48,475
- 22%: $48,476 to $103,350
- 24%: $103,351 to $197,300
- 32%: $197,301 to $250,525
- 35%: $250,526 to $626,350
- 37%: over $626,350

States with no income tax: Alaska, Florida, Nevada, New Hampshire, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, Washington, Wyoming

## Intended Users
- US employees calculating expected take-home pay
- Job seekers comparing salary offers after taxes
- Freelancers and self-employed individuals estimating net income
- HR professionals explaining paycheck deductions to employees
- Students and recent graduates entering the workforce
- Anyone trying to understand their paycheck deductions
